  <section v="15">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the difference between Torah and mitzvos, where mitzvos are performed as a servant, while Torah study in a state of self-nullification makes one like the King Himself, as the words of G-d speak through him.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">And 4)</t>
    <t s="2">And this will be understood by prefacing what our Rebbe, the Alter Rebbe, explains</t>
    <t s="3">(the Baal HaGeulah of Yud-Tes Kislev89)</t>
    <t s="4">in Torah Ohr, the discourse beginning "Vayeishev Yaakov b'Eretz Megurei Aviv"90</t>
    <t s="5">regarding the difference between Torah and mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="6">that in the fulfillment of mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="7">the person who fulfills the mitzvos is in the category of a servant,</t>
    <t s="8">like a servant who fulfills the king's command and does his bidding,</t>
    <t s="9">but not so in the study of Torah, where he is the king himself91,</t>
    <t s="10">as per the statement92</t>
    <t s="11">"Who are the kings? The Rabbis."</t>
    <t s="12">For when his engagement in Torah is in a state of self-nullification (bittul),</t>
    <t s="13">then "I place My words in your mouth"93,</t>
    <t s="14">My actual words,</t>
    <t s="15">meaning</t>
    <t s="16">(it is not the person who speaks,</t>
    <t s="17">but rather)</t>
    <t s="18">that "the word of G-d, this is the halachah"94</t>
    <t s="19">is itself revealed within him and it speaks from his throat.</t>
    <t s="20">And this is "Who are the kings? The Rabbis,"</t>
    <t s="21">for because their study of the halachos is in a state of self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="22">their study of the halachos is in a manner that the King Himself</t>
    <t s="23">(the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He)</t>
    <t s="24">decrees and speaks the ruling</t>
    <t s="25">(the halachah).</t>
    <t s="26">And he continues there,</t>
    <t s="27">that this is the meaning of "Vayeishev Yaakov b'Eretz Megurei Aviv,"</t>
    <t s="28">"Megurei" is an expression of awe (yirah)95</t>
    <t s="29">and also an expression of a storehouse (otzar)</t>
    <t s="30">[like "a granary (megurah) filled with produce"96,</t>
    <t s="31">which is a vessel in which one stores things],</t>
    <t s="32">and both align with one another, as it is written97</t>
    <t s="33">"The awe of G-d is His storehouse," and likewise in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory98</t>
    <t s="34">"a storehouse of fear of Heaven."</t>
    <t s="35">[And this explanation was written by the Maggid99</t>
    <t s="36">(the Baal HaHilula of Yud-Tes Kislev100)</t>
    <t s="37">in Ohr HaTorah101</t>
    <t s="38">that "Megurei Aviv" is the awe of his Father in Heaven,</t>
    <t s="39">and in the continuation of the topic there102</t>
    <t s="40">: "Megurei" is an expression of gathering and ingathering, like "one who gathers (oger)103</t>
    <t s="41">in the summer."]</t>
    <t s="42">And the explanation of "Megurei Aviv" is,</t>
    <t s="43">that the self-nullification of awe (yirah)</t>
    <t s="44">[and particularly the self-nullification of sublime awe (yirah ila'ah)]</t>
    <t s="45">is a vessel of reception</t>
    <t s="46">[a storehouse]</t>
    <t s="47">for the revelation of supernal wisdom (Chochmah Ila'ah)</t>
    <t s="48">[for supernal wisdom is called "his father" (aviv)104].</t>
    <t s="49">And as above,</t>
    <t s="50">that when his engagement in Torah is in a state of self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="51">then "I place My words in your mouth,"</t>
    <t s="52">that "the word of G-d, this is the halachah," speaks from his throat.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="16">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the self-nullification of awe described as "Megurei Aviv" is the self-nullification of a son, not a servant, which enables a perfect and absolute bittul where one has no independent existence.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">A)</t>
    <t s="2">Now, from the explanation in Torah Ohr that the self-nullification of awe, which is a vessel for supernal wisdom, is called "Megurei Aviv,"</t>
    <t s="3">meaning that the Holy One, blessed be He, is referred to here not with the title "Master" (Adon) but with the title "Father" (Av)</t>
    <t s="4">[as per the language of the Maggid that "Megurei Aviv" is the awe of his Father in Heaven],</t>
    <t s="5">it is understood from this,</t>
    <t s="6">that this self-nullification is</t>
    <t s="7">(not the self-nullification of a servant,</t>
    <t s="8">but rather)</t>
    <t s="9">the self-nullification of a son,</t>
    <t s="10">and through this self-nullification</t>
    <t s="11">(of a son),</t>
    <t s="12">"the word of G-d, this is the halachah, is itself revealed within him and it speaks from his throat,"</t>
    <t s="13">for in the service of the category of a son, it is possible to have a truly absolute self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="14">where he has no independent existence at all, and his entire existence is the existence of the father.</t>
    <t s="15">[And as explained in Likkutei Torah105,</t>
    <t s="16">that the fact that souls are called "sons" is not like a son below, who, although he is taken from his father's brain, is later separate from him</t>
    <t s="17">(therefore, his lost object and his father's lost object, his lost object takes precedence106),</t>
    <t s="18">but rather,</t>
    <t s="19">the soul is completely one (kula chad) and is not separate from Him, blessed be He, at all].</t>
    <t s="20">Moreover,</t>
    <t s="21">this self-nullification is superior to the self-nullification of a servant,</t>
    <t s="22">and even more so, as above</t>
    <t s="23">(from Torah Ohr)</t>
    <t s="24">that through engaging in Torah with self-nullification, he is not like a servant fulfilling the king's command, but rather he is the king himself.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="17">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the service of Torah scholars, called "sons," is to gather and elevate holy sparks, bringing peace to the world and to themselves, as their self-nullification allows them to experience the pleasure of the Creator.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">B)</t>
    <t s="2">And this is "And all your children (banayich) shall be students of G-d, and great shall be the peace of your children (banayich)" — do not read "banayich" (your children) but "bonayich" (your builders)</t>
    <t s="3">(and it continues)</t>
    <t s="4">"Great peace have those who love Your Torah,"</t>
    <t s="5">that the service of the Torah scholars, who are called "sons"</t>
    <t s="6">(banayich)</t>
    <t s="7">is as the Maggid's explanation102</t>
    <t s="8">on the verse "Vayeishev Yaakov b'Eretz Megurei Aviv"</t>
    <t s="9">(which is the matter of the service of the category of sons,</t>
    <t s="10">as above)</t>
    <t s="11">"to gather and collect the holy sparks and to bring them in and elevate them upward."</t>
    <t s="12">[For this is also what continues in the verse "in the land of Canaan,"</t>
    <t s="13">Canaan being an expression of a merchant (sochar),</t>
    <t s="14">that the purpose of the soul's descent below is "to acquire for itself merchandise and acquisition specifically in this world"107</t>
    <t s="15">through the sparks that it refines,</t>
    <t s="16">and this is also what continues in the parshah108</t>
    <t s="17">"And behold, we were binding sheaves (me'al'mim alumim),"</t>
    <t s="18">which refers to the refinement of the sparks109].</t>
    <t s="19">And through this, "Vayeishev Yaakov"</t>
    <t s="20">(Yaakov sought110</t>
    <t s="21">to dwell)</t>
    <t s="22">in tranquility — the matter of peace (shalom),</t>
    <t s="23">both the peace in the world, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said: "Torah scholars increase peace in the world,"</t>
    <t s="24">and also peace for the Torah scholars themselves,</t>
    <t s="25">as it continues, "Great peace have those who love Your Torah,"</t>
    <t s="26">for since the Torah scholars, called "sons," are in a state of absolute self-nullification, as above,</t>
    <t s="27">therefore, the category of the satisfaction (nachas ruach) of the Creator, from the fact that they increase peace in the world, is also drawn down to the Torah scholars themselves.</t>
    <t s="28">And this is "Great peace have those who love Your Torah,"</t>
    <t s="29">that because their service in Torah and mitzvos is</t>
    <t s="30">(not in order to receive reward,</t>
    <t s="31">but rather)</t>
    <t s="32">out of love for G-d,</t>
    <t s="33">to bring satisfaction (nachas ruach) to the Creator</t>
    <t s="34">[and they know that their reward,</t>
    <t s="35">the satisfaction of the created being,</t>
    <t s="36">is</t>
    <t s="37">(as above, section 8)</t>
    <t s="38">incomparable to the satisfaction of the Creator],</t>
    <t s="39">behold, through this self-nullification, the satisfaction and delight of the Creator is drawn down to them in revelation,</t>
    <t s="40">for since they have no independent existence at all,</t>
    <t s="41">the delight of the Creator is their delight.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
